newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai leader arrives in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Thai leader arrives in Singapore.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh arrived in Singapore on Thursday for a two-day visit aimed at boosting ties and eliminating what he called image problems.

"Singapore is considered among our closest friends," Chavalit said in an interview with the Singapore's Strait Times newspaper published on Thursday. "We deem our relations with Singapore as one of Thailand's most important economic partners, a vital one."
But Chavalit said there was an "image problem" that coloured the views of people from both nations and should be eliminated.

"We in Thailand would not wish Singaporeans to consider us as inefficient," he said. "On the other hand, I believe that Singaporeans would not like it if their Thai counterparts think of them only as unfriendly competitors."
Singapore is Thailand's most important trading partner in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), which also includes Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam.
Two way-trade reached an estimated US$7.7 to $11.5 billion last year. There are also 50,000 Thai workers in Singapore, most of them in the construction industry.
